sections.hypothesis: Weeks after the Crypto Fear & Greed Index read Extreme Fear (below 25) return more than other weeks, by more than costs.
sections.rationale: Economic reason: in extreme fear, forced and panicked sellers accept low prices, and patient buyers are paid for taking the other side. Outside evidence is mixed and partly against: Kestrel's own Fear & Greed contrarian strategy failed badly (+20% against +1,087% holding BTC), selling the start of bull runs and buying the start of bear markets, and the volatile-spell study found falls in volatile spells kept falling. This study asks the narrower question that strategy didn't: does the week after extreme fear do better than other weeks? Luke chose this study (2026-11-14).
sections.rules: kestrel signal-study extreme-fear BTCUSDT ETHUSDT --research <this note>: daily bars before 2025-11-01; at each Sunday close, the signal is on when the Fear & Greed value known at the close (kestrel.data.sentiment: a value is known from the day after its stamp) is below 25; outcome: log return from that close to the next Sunday's; weeks with a missing bar or no value are skipped. The index starts 2018-02.
sections.falsification: PROCEED only if P(spread > 0) is at least 90% and the spread (mean week after extreme fear minus other weeks) is above 0.22%; otherwise KILL, and no strategy is built. Run once.
sections.parameters: Sunday closes (UTC), the next 7 days, BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT 1d, pooled; 5,000 bootstrap resamples; no setting chosen after looking.
sections.costs: Hurdle 0.22%: one round trip of the taker fee and half-spread from kestrel.toml. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings.
